subject: FW: 250952-LPSG ADA2 Habit Burger # 53511
body:
Hi Fernando,



Happy Monday and thank you for speaking with me this morning.



I’m forwarding this thread regarding the required $300 engineering review for the signage at the Hurley Building (Willo Historic District).


As outlined in my email below, our request is based on the existing installation’s long-term proven stability, with no new forces or modifications being introduced. We believe this may qualify for consideration under engineering judgment—a practice in which determinations are made based on observed conditions and historical performance when full structural visibility isn’t possible. 

For reference, I’ve attached our observation report.


Would you be able to review this request and advise whether the requirement can be waived, or let us know the proper process and contact for a formal appeal?


Thank you for your time and consideration.


Best regards,

 

Steve Skye

Hi Tony,

Thank you for the update and for outlining the next steps for the signage review at the Hurley Building.


In regard to the required $300 engineering review, I’d like to inquire whether there is any flexibility to waive this requirement based on existing conditions. As noted in the attached observation report (provided for reference only), the signage in question is being reinstalled in an existing location that has previously demonstrated long-term structural stability. The footing and anchoring system—while not directly observable—show no evidence of failure, movement, or deterioration, and the sign has performed adequately under real-world conditions.


Our evaluation supports the conclusion that the current installation remains structurally sound, and no material changes to its configuration or load distribution are being introduced. For these reasons, we respectfully ask if this requirement may be waived under engineering judgment.


If a formal appeal is required, could you please advise us who to contact or what documentation would need to be submitted?


Appreciate your time and guidance.

subject: U-Haul Thatcher – Zoning & Sign Code Summary (08/08/25)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I wanted to update you on the U-Haul Thatcher project (2629 W US Highway 70, Thatcher, AZ – Job #27325).


The property is zoned C-2 – Highway Commercial, which permits general retail, service businesses, auto rental, and similar commercial uses. Based on the Town of Thatcher’s zoning ordinance, here are the key sign code highlights for this site:

*	Total Signage Limit: 84 sq ft per business
*	Wall Signs: 1 sq ft per 2 linear ft of building frontage
*	Freestanding Signs: Max 64 sq ft area, 18 ft height, address must be included
*	Window Signage: Limited to 25% of window area
*	Awning/Projecting/Shingle Signs: Allowed with specific restrictions
*	Directional Signs: Max 6 sq ft, 3 ft high; no advertising
*	Prohibited: Billboards, roof signs, flashing/animated displays, and signs over the ROW unless expressly permitted


I've attached a formal zoning and sign ordinance report for your reference. I’ll follow up with the Town of Thatcher Planning Department on Monday (08/11) to confirm any site-specific interpretations, as they are closed on Fridays.


Let me know if you need anything else in the meantime.


Best regards,

Thanks for sending the markups over.

 

We’ve reviewed the attached file, and while it includes some basic measurements, it unfortunately won’t satisfy the requirements of the Anthem Community Council or Maricopa County for permitting purposes. subject: RE: Tempe Birth Center
body:
Hi Jessica,



I just wanted to follow up on our recent correspondence regarding signage at Tempe Birth Center.


As noted by the City of Tempe, the property is zoned CC and is classified as a National Historic site. Because of this, any proposed signage—such as the 3 ft x 5 ft non-illuminated, double-sided monument sign you mentioned—would need to be reviewed not only under the standard sign code but also by the Historic Preservation Office.


At this point, we’d be happy to continue looking into what will be required to move forward with a sign that aligns with both the City’s signage allowances and historic preservation standards. 

This would likely involve preparing a conceptual rendering and submitting it to Zachary Lechner, the Historic Preservation Officer, for preliminary feedback.


Before we take that next step, we wanted to check in and see if you're ready to proceed. Some of these requirements may be straightforward—or may involve additional steps—so we want to ensure you're comfortable with exploring it further.


Please let me know how you’d like to proceed, and we’ll be happy to assist.


Warm regards,

 

Steve Skye

Hi Taylor,

We’ve reviewed the City of Mesa’s plan review comments and have outlined the required corrections below. Attached is the Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP – BOA20-00484), which governs signage allowances for this development.

 

📏 Frontage Dimensions
The city is requesting that the lineal frontage of the tenant space be clearly shown on the site plan.
• If the suite fronts more than one street, both dimensions must be provided.
• This is needed to confirm the correct sign area allowance per Mesa Zoning Code §11-50-3.


📐 CSP Compliance
The signage must adhere to the maximum number of signs and total square footage allowed under the CSP.
• For example, tenant spaces with 81–199 feet of frontage may have up to 4 signs with a maximum aggregate area of 200 sq ft (160 base + 10 sq ft bonus per sign).
• Each sign must remain at or below 160 sq ft, and sign width must not exceed 80% of the wall elevation.


🖼️ Legibility
The city noted that some verbiage and images in the original submittal were blurry or difficult to read. Please ensure all text and graphic elements are crisp and high-resolution.


📎 Complete Plan Set
We’ll handle uploading a complete revised plan set for resubmittal once the updated files are received. Partial or single-sheet uploads will not be accepted by the city.

• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage

 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

1.	Scaled Site Plan – Showing the monument sign’s location relative to property lines, setbacks, utility boxes, easements, driveways, and visibility triangles.

4.	Color & Material Schedule – A clearly labeled legend or callouts identifying all materials and colors (e.g., Pantone or 3M vinyl codes, paint finishes).
5.	Architectural Context – The site plan should also show adjacent drive lanes, building edges, or other relevant features for context.
6.	Photographic Rendering (optional but helpful) – A photo simulation of the sign at the proposed location, if available.


These items are required for a complete ACC submittal and must be addressed before the application can be accepted for formal review.

Hope you're doing well — after reviewing the artwork in light of the Anthem Community Council’s (ACC) requirements, I’ve identified a few items we’ll need to finalize to complete the submittal.

🔍 Summary of What’s Needed:

1.	Scaled Site Plan – Showing the monument sign’s location relative to property lines, setbacks, utility boxes, easements, driveways, and visibility triangles.
2.	Landscaping Plan – If any existing landscaping is being removed or impacted, we’ll need to note that and show replacement species, sizes, and placement. If not, we can indicate that no changes are proposed.
3.	Vertical Section Cut – A technical side-view detail through the sign showing structure, base/foundation, internal framing, and material thicknesses.
4.	Color & Material Schedule – A clearly labeled legend or callouts identifying all materials and colors (e.g., Pantone or 3M vinyl codes, paint finishes).
5.	Architectural Context – The site plan should also show adjacent drive lanes, building edges, or other relevant features for context.
6.	Photographic Rendering (optional but helpful) – A photo simulation of the sign at the proposed location, if available.


These items are required for a complete ACC submittal and must be addressed before the application can be accepted for formal review.


Let’s schedule a quick call to go over this together and determine how you'd like to proceed — whether we assist directly with the drawing updates or coordinate through your design team.

Hi Kyle,

I’ve spoken directly with Maricopa County regarding the requirements for the preview and menu boards at the Wendy’s site in Anthem (3422 W Anthem Way, Parcel #203-04-534). Below is a summary of the key regulations and submittal items:

 

________________________________

📋 Code Requirements (per Zoning Chapter 14, Section 1403.2.4):
• Only 1 preview and 1 menu board are permitted per site.
• Maximum height: 7' to the top of the structure
• Maximum area: 32 sq ft per board
• Must be screened from street view
• Must be at least 200 ft from any residential property
• Internally illuminated boards must show a disconnect switch on the plans
• Boards cannot include audible or animated features visible to the street

________________________________

🧾 Required Submittal Documents (per County checklist):
• Permit Application – including current parcel number
• 7 site plans showing:
 – Board locations & setbacks
 – Existing signage
 – North arrow, scale, and landscaping
 – Driveway triangle if near entry/exit
• 3 construction sets with:
 – Elevations with board dimensions and mounting
 – Electrical details (disconnect location per NEC)
 – Plan view if double-faced
• Grading and Drainage Plan sealed by AZ Civil Engineer
• Photometric data if signs are illuminated
• Acknowledgement of financial responsibility

________________________________

📎 Attached are two County documents for your reference: the full signage packet and Chapter 14 zoning ordinance.

We recommend including the disconnect article in the electrical plans and clearly identifying code references on the drawings to streamline approval.


Please review these details and confirm if Telaid will provide updated specs or if you’d like Christy Signs to coordinate plan preparation.


Let me know if you need anything clarified.

body:
Hi Kyle,



Hope you're doing well — after reviewing the artwork in light of the Anthem Community Council’s (ACC) requirements, I’ve identified a few items we’ll need to finalize to complete the submittal.



🔍 Summary of What’s Needed:

1.	Scaled Site Plan – Showing the monument sign’s location relative to property lines, setbacks, utility boxes, easements, driveways, and visibility triangles.
2.	Landscaping Plan – If any existing landscaping is being removed or impacted, we’ll need to note that and show replacement species, sizes, and placement. If not, we can indicate that no changes are proposed.
3.	Vertical Section Cut – A technical side-view detail through the sign showing structure, base/foundation, internal framing, and material thicknesses.
4.	Color & Material Schedule – A clearly labeled legend or callouts identifying all materials and colors (e.g., Pantone or 3M vinyl codes, paint finishes).
5.	Architectural Context – The site plan should also show adjacent drive lanes, building edges, or other relevant features for context.
6.	Photographic Rendering (optional but helpful) – A photo simulation of the sign at the proposed location, if available.


These items are required for a complete ACC submittal and must be addressed before the application can be accepted for formal review.


Let’s schedule a quick call to go over this together and determine how you'd like to proceed — whether we assist directly with the drawing updates or coordinate through your design team.


Looking forward to your thoughts.

body:
Hi Frank,

Happy Friday !

We received an automated notice from Maricopa County this morning indicating there has been no recent activity on Permit No. BLDC2600111 and that the permit remains under review (see below).

As discussed previously, we are still awaiting the revised permit package. We want to make sure everything is addressed properly before the next submittal to hopefully avoid another review cycle.

To "measure twice and cut once," I previously provided the County redlines along with a sample Maricopa County sign permit package showing additional code and NEC reference information that has been required on other County projects.

While I do not specifically see the current reviewer calling out the following items:

• Maricopa County adopted code references
• NEC Article 600 notes
• Branch circuit / disconnect language

we have encountered situations where these items were later requested during subsequent review cycles even though they were not identified in the initial correction comments.

The sample package included examples of supplemental information previously accepted by the County, including:

• 2018 IBC references
• 2017 NEC references
• NEC Article 600 disconnect requirements
• Branch circuit requirements
• Grounding and bonding notes

The primary comments still appear to be focused on providing a definite and complete design, including mounting hardware, wall attachment details, foundation information, engineering clarification, and elimination of TBD conditions within the permit set.

We simply want to make sure the next resubmittal is as complete as possible before it is returned to the County.

Please give me a call when you have a chance so we can discuss the status of the revisions and determine if there is anything further, we can do to assist.

Thank you,

body:
Hi Thomas,



Attached is our preliminary zoning report for the Fantastico's Mexican Food property located at 4985 N Sunland Gin Road in Eloy.


Our initial review indicates that the property is zoned C-2 General Commercial, which generally supports commercial tenant identification signage, including wall signs, monument signs, and illuminated signage. The report also summarizes the applicable sign ordinance provisions and permitting requirements identified during our research.


At this stage, the report is intended to provide a preliminary overview of the zoning and sign regulations applicable to the site. The final allowable sign area has not yet been calculated and will require verification of the building frontage, street frontage, existing site signage, and any applicable setback conditions.


Our next step will be to complete a detailed sign compliance analysis and determine the maximum allowable signage available for the property based on the City's frontage-based calculations.

subject: Bel Fleur Sign Installation – Punch List & Revised Artwork (06/15/26)
body:
Hi Veronica and Kevin,



Thank you for taking the time to meet with our Shop Foreman, Scott, on site to review the installation concerns.


Following Scott's site visit and discussion with Kevin, our team has reviewed the items identified and developed a corrective plan to address the concerns raised during the installation review.


Attached is a revised drawing showing a proposed aluminum wireway to be installed on the back side of the monument wall. The wireway will be approximately 2" deep and 9'-0" long and will be painted to match the wall color. The existing power supply box will be relocated inside the wireway to conceal the electrical components and wiring. Rigid conduit will then be routed from the wireway down the wall, underground, and over to the existing electrical source.


In addition to the wireway installation, our punch list includes the following:

• Relocate the power supply into the new wireway enclosure.
• Conceal and secure exposed wiring.
• Repair locations where wire sleeves were cut short.
• Add additional anchor points to the larger letter where needed.
• Clean up and touch up silicone application for a more consistent appearance.
• Secure loose wiring and complete final installation detailing.
• Restore and paint all new work to match adjacent surfaces.


We believe this approach will provide the cleanest and most professional finished appearance while addressing the concerns discussed on site.


Before proceeding, we would like to provide the attached drawing for your review and HOA approval. Once approval is received, we will schedule the corrective work and complete the remaining punch list items.


Please review the attached drawing and let us know if you have any questions or comments.

subject: Comprehensive Sign Plan and Sign Permit Review Process (06/15/26)
body:
Good afternoon, Larry,



Thank you for speaking with me previously concerning the U-Haul project in Green Valley.


We are evaluating the signage entitlement strategy for the proposed U-Haul facility in Green Valley and would appreciate your guidance regarding the review process.


Our understanding is that the site currently appears capable of supporting a code-compliant signage package within the standard sign area allowances. However, the owner is also considering a Comprehensive Sign Plan to request additional sign area and flexibility beyond the standard code.


When speaking with Building Safety, we were advised that once a sign permit is approved, a Comprehensive Sign Plan may no longer be an option. We are wondering if this may have been a misunderstanding and would appreciate clarification from the Planning Division.


Specifically, is it permissible to pursue a phased approach whereby:

1.	A sign permit application is submitted and reviewed based upon signage that complies with the current code allowances; and
2.	A Comprehensive Sign Plan application is submitted concurrently or subsequently to seek approval of additional signage beyond those allowances.


In other words, would approval of a standard sign permit preclude the property owner from later pursuing a Comprehensive Sign Plan for additional signage, or can the two processes proceed independently provided that any additional signage is not installed until the CSP is approved?


We appreciate any guidance you can provide regarding the preferred process and sequencing for these applications.


Thank you for your time and assistance.


Best regards,

 

Steve Skye

Hi Sam,



Thank you for the detailed response and for looking into this matter. Your insight regarding the existing freeway pylon sign being potentially legal non-conforming is extremely helpful.


Based on your comments, I am thinking the most prudent next step may be to obtain the original permit records for the freeway sign before evaluating potential modifications. My thought is that the original permit package may contain:



• Approved sign dimensions
• Structural and engineering information
• Foundation details
• Wind-load criteria
• Original sign area calculations


Having that information would allow us to better understand the existing structure and determine what modifications may be feasible while preserving the sign's legal non-conforming status. It would also help us evaluate whether a cabinet replacement or EMC retrofit could be accomplished without triggering concerns associated with substantial structural modifications.


Are you aware of the best way to request copies of the original sign permit records for this property?


Additionally, does this seem like a reasonable approach from the City's perspective before pursuing a formal sign concept?


Our thought process is to first understand the original approved structure so that any proposed modifications can be designed within the existing structural and permitting framework to the greatest extent possible.


Thank you again for your assistance and guidance. We appreciate your help with this project.


Best regards,

From: Samuel Leonard <samuel.leonard@EloyAZ.gov> 
Sent: Monday, June 15, 2026 6:08 PM
To: Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com>
Cc: bpsss@icloud.com
Subject: RE: Fantastico's Mexican Food – Signage Research Follow-Up (06/15/26)

 

Good afternoon,

 

I’ve been looking into this and talking with our Director of Community Development. It seems that the freeway pylon sign could be Legal non-conforming, and as such, we would likely allow signage in the existing cabinet. As for Electronic Message Center signs, we would likely allow this, so long as it meets the requirements in Eloy City Code - 21-4-3.9 C. 

 

I’m not able to say for sure if something would be approved or not until a formal submittal is made, but if you are just looking to insert an EMC into the existing cabinet with little to no modifications to the existing structure, it is reasonable that the city would support that. If you need to start making more intensive improvements to the existing structure then there may be additional considerations that need to be addressed. If for some reason the existing structure would need to be replaced or heavily modified, it’s reasonable to believe that it would lose it’s legal non-conforming status and would need to be brought up to current sign standards, which would not allow for a freeway pylon sign.

 

Let me know if you have any other questions.
Sam

 

 

 

 

Some notes to keep in mind:

 

City Sign Code: https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-9920

 

21-8-4.3: LOSS OF NONCONFORMING STATUS:

If a nonconforming use of land or a nonconforming use of a conforming structure is discontinued for a continuous period of six (6) months, the rights to a legal nonconforming status shall terminate. The initial decision as to whether a prior existing, non-conforming use has been abandoned shall be made by the Zoning Administrator. Such decision may be appealed to the Board of Adjustment by the affected property owner within ninety (90) calendar days of the ruling by the Zoning Administrator following the procedures under section 21-6-11.8 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-11111#JD_21-6-11.8> , "Appeal", of this chapter. (Ord. 18-880, 7-23-2018)

 

 

  21-4-3.9 - C.   Electronic Message Center: Electronic message center (EMC) signs are permitted as identified in section 21-4-3.8 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-10023#JD_21-4-3.8> , table 4.3-1 of this section 21-4-3 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-9920#JD_21-4-3> , subject to the conditions identified below:

      1.   EMC signs shall be counted as a portion of the total aggregate sign area.

      2.   Signs must be entirely located on-site.

      3.   There shall be no moving or flashing green or red features that could be mistaken as traffic control devices.

      4.   Digital message portion of the sign shall not exceed fifty percent (50%) of sign area.

      5.   Sign shall be installed at least one hundred fifty feet (150') from a designated crosswalk.

      6.   Sign shall not be installed within three hundred fifty feet (350') of a residential structure.

      7.   EMC signs shall be separated from other EMC signs by a minimum of one thousand feet (1,000').

      8.   All continuous loop image progression occurring on the face or copy of the sign must have a minimum interval time of eight (8) seconds.

      9.   All EMC signs shall have automatic dimming controls, either by photocell (hardwired) or via software settings, to reduce the illumination intensity of the sign as ambient lighting conditions change.

 

G.   Freeway Pylon Signs: Freeway pylon signs are permitted as identified in section 21-4-3.8 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-10023#JD_21-4-3.8> , table 4.3-1 of this section 21-4-3 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-9920#JD_21-4-3> , subject to the conditions identified below:

      1.   All freeway pylon signs shall be part of a comprehensive sign package that requires both review and recommendation by Planning and Zoning Commission and approval by the City Council.

      2.   Freeway pylon signs shall be counted as a portion of the total aggregate sign area.

      3.   One freestanding pylon sign shall be allowed per property; additional signs are allowed on a property with street frontage that exceeds two hundred feet (200'). If multiple signs are placed on a single street frontage, there shall be a minimum of one hundred feet (100') between each sign.

      4.   A freestanding pylon identification sign may be placed on Commercially or Industrially zoned property that has a minimum of three hundred feet (300') of freeway frontage. In order to apply for a freeway pylon sign, the site, or combination of sites, must be at least twenty (20) acres in size and the sign should identify multiple tenants (a maximum of 4 tenants) or a combined minimum of two hundred thousand (200,000) square feet of office, retail, or manufacturing space.

      5.   Sign copy shall be limited to name and/or logo identification with approved directional information.

      6.   The pylon identification sign shall not exceed an overall height of eighty feet (80') above the natural grade of the site; has a maximum width of twelve feet (12'), or a maximum depth of four feet (4').

      7.   Pylon signs shall not be located closer than a distance equal to the height of the sign from the freeway right-of-way. A minimum separation distance of three hundred feet (300') shall be observed between any such freeway pylon signs located on the same side of the freeway.

      8.   A total maximum sign area of six hundred (600) square feet; with any one panel not exceeding one hundred fifty (150) square feet in area, plus the center identification.

      9.   Pylon signs may not be installed on a parcel, lot or development site that has an existing billboard or other prohibited sign.

      10.   Council, when considering the required comprehensive sign package, may vary restrictions pertaining to height, sign copy, and separation distance upon appropriate justification presented by the applicant, such as, but not limited to, identification of regional or community centers or conveying a civic or public interest message.

      11.   Sign supports shall consist of at least thirty percent (30%) of the total sign width; each single support shall consist of at least fifteen percent (15%) of the total sign width.

      12.   Signs shall be composed of a decorative base, support, and sign face.

subject: U-Haul Green Valley – CSP Discussion with Town of Sahuarita (06/16/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I spoke with Larry Myers of the Town of Sahuarita Planning Division regarding the proposed CSP strategy.


Key points:

*	I-19-facing elevations may qualify for a 25% sign area increase above the standard allowance.
*	The east elevation (Sign 8) is the only elevation eligible for this bonus.
*	A CSP allows only a 20% increase and is strictly applied.
*	Unused sign area cannot be transferred from one elevation to another.
*	A CSP and sign permit application may be submitted concurrently.
*	If the CSP is approved later, a separate permit application would be required for the existing and additional signs approved through the CSP.


After reviewing the current sign area calculations, only Building A – South Elevation exceeds the allowable sign area, with 292 SF proposed where 225 SF is allowed (67 SF over).


Larry's opinion was that he does not see a practical path to permit the entire proposed sign inventory as currently designed and recommends revising the package to comply with the 
Town's sign code limitations.


I've attached a summary report for reference.


Best,

Thank you for taking the time to meet with our Shop Foreman, Scott, on site to review the installation concerns.


Following Scott's site visit and discussion with Kevin, our team has reviewed the items identified and developed a corrective plan to address the concerns raised during the installation review.


Attached is a revised drawing showing a proposed aluminum wireway to be installed on the back side of the monument wall. The existing power supply box will be relocated inside the wireway to conceal the electrical components and wiring. Rigid conduit will then be routed from the wireway down the wall, underground, and over to the existing electrical source.


In addition to the wireway installation, our punch list includes the following:

• Relocate the power supply into the new wireway enclosure.
• Conceal and secure exposed wiring.
• Repair locations where wire sleeves were cut short.
• Add additional anchor points to the larger letter where needed.
• Clean up and touch up silicone application for a more consistent appearance.
• Secure loose wiring and complete final installation detailing.
• Restore and paint all new work to match adjacent surfaces.


We believe this approach will provide the cleanest and most professional finished appearance while addressing the concerns discussed on site.


Before proceeding, we would like to provide the attached drawing for your review and HOA approval. Once approval is received, we will schedule the corrective work and complete the remaining punch list items.

subject: AFC Med/Chiro – Permit Extension & Final Inspection Compliance (06/18/26)
body:
Management Team,



We have received confirmation from the City of Surprise that Permit No. 2021003988 has been extended through July 17, 2026, to allow completion of the required final inspections and permit closeout.


While this is a positive development, I believe it is important to recognize the significance of the City's response. This permit dates to 2021 and would ordinarily be considered well beyond a typical inspection and closeout timeline. The City exercised administrative discretion in granting an extension rather than requiring additional permitting action.


This situation also serves as a reminder that permit issuance alone does not complete a project. Final inspections and permit closeout remain critical components of the permitting process. Jurisdictions may not be willing to provide similar accommodations on future projects where permits remain open for extended periods without completion.


Given the age of this permit and the City's request for prompt action, I recommend we prioritize completion of the required inspections and continue monitoring other open permits to ensure final inspections are not overlooked.


Best,

Hi Mackenzie,



That is one option, however I do not believe the city is specifically requiring a site-specific engineered sign package at this time.


The reviewer's comment allows for either:

• ASA (Arizona Sign Association) Engineering Standards demonstrating compliance with the 2018 IBC, or
• Engineering calculations based on the 2018 IBC.


We can provide the ASA engineering worksheets and supporting documentation, which is typically a more economical approach than obtaining a sealed engineering package and stamped calculations for the sign.


I am not certain what the cost would be for the ASA documentation at this time and would need to discuss it with our estimator. However, I would expect it to be less expensive than obtaining a sealed engineering package.


Please let us know if you would be interested in pursuing the ASA compliance method, or if you already have an engineer involved and would prefer to provide a sealed engineering package instead.


Best regards,

subject: RE: Habit Burger # 65027 (27782) – Glendale Correction Comments (06/22/26)
body:
Hi Taylor,



Thank you for sending the revised Brand Book. 


Regarding the monument sign comment, I do not believe the city is necessarily stating that the monument sign is located within the right-of-way. Rather, the reviewer appears to be requesting that the property line and right-of-way limits be clearly shown on the site plan so they can verify the sign is located on private property.


Currently, the site plan identifies the monument sign location, but it does not appear to show the property boundary or provide dimensions demonstrating the sign's setback from the property line. Without that information, Planning cannot confirm compliance and has therefore issued the comment that no signs are permitted within the public right-of-way.


My recommendation would be to revise the site plan to clearly identify:
• Property line and right-of-way line
• Monument sign location
• Setback dimension from the sign to the property line/right-of-way


Once that information is provided, the reviewer should be able to determine whether the monument sign complies with the City's requirements.


The other Planning comments appear to relate to sign area calculations and the overall height of the drive-thru signage.


Please let me know if you have any questions.


Best regards,

subject: RE: Burger King #16449 – Permit Resubmittal Requirement (06/22/26)
body:
Hi Joshua,



Thank you for following up.


Based on my last discussion with Pinal County, it appears that the variance and separate CSP review are no longer required for this location. However, there were still a few items the County requested before the permit can move back into review.


The primary item is a sign criteria analysis demonstrating compliance with the 2006 CSP requirements for the site. Specifically, the County requested:

• Building frontage dimensions for each elevation containing signage
• Sign area calculations for each elevation
• A summary of the total proposed sign area
• An explanation showing how the frontage measurements and sign area calculations were derived


The County advised that sign allowances are based on building frontage at a rate of 2 square feet of sign area per linear foot of frontage.


I reviewed the latest Brand Book package and did not see a frontage calculation worksheet or sign area analysis included. Unless those calculations are contained in a separate document, I believe that is the remaining information needed before we can place the application back into review.


If you have frontage dimensions and sign area calculations available, please send them over and I can review them against the County's requirements. If not, we can discuss the best way to prepare the required documentation and move the permit forward.


Best regards,

 

Steve Skye
Permit Acquisitions

subject: Chick-fil-A & AZP Monument Sign Review – City of Chandler Summary (06/23/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



He is a summary of the email thread (see below) and the guidance we received from the City of Chandler regarding the proposed monument sign arrangement at Desert Palms (Alma School & Warner).


Background

AZP originally asked whether the development could support separate monument signs for Chick-fil-A and other pad users if the parcels were ultimately split into separate ownership parcels. The concept evolved into a proposal consisting of:

• A separate Chick-fil-A monument sign
• A separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign
• Approximately 302 feet of separation between the two proposed signs


City Review

I contacted Chandler and provided the site plan for review. Joe Sauer with Chandler Development Services discussed the proposal with Planning and provided their position.


City's Position

Planning has indicated that they will not support individual tenant monument signs for these parcels. Instead, they will only consider approval of multi-tenant monument signs that conform to the remodeled sign program criteria.

The city indicated:

• Two (2) new multi-tenant monument signs can be accommodated in the corridor.
• The signs must be spaced a minimum of approximately 275 feet apart.
• Based on the site layout, there appears to be room for two signs between the existing 14-foot monument sign and the western property limits.
• The new signs must generally match the approved multi-tenant sign design and be permitted as duplicate structures.


Flexibility Within the Tenant Panels

The most important item from Joe's comments is that while the structures themselves must remain multi-tenant signs, the tenant panels may be arranged at the discretion of the property manager.

Examples provided by the city include:

• A major tenant could occupy the area of two or three standard panels.
• Panel configurations may be adjusted to accommodate tenant needs.
• Background panel colors must remain compliant with the sign criteria (white backgrounds).
• Corporate colors are permitted only in the copy and graphics.
• Copy is expected to be routed and push thru.


Conclusion

The city does not appear willing to approve separate Chick-fil-A and AZP monument signs as standalone tenant signs. However, they are willing to allow two new multi-tenant monument signs, and there appears to be considerable flexibility in how the tenant panels are allocated within those signs.

This may provide a practical path forward while remaining consistent with the City's sign program requirements.


Please let me know if you would like to discuss further.


Best regards,

Hi Rocky,

I reviewed the Chandler Sign Code along with the site plan provided.


Based on the plan, the proposed Chick-fil-A monument sign and the AZP multi-tenant monument sign appear to be separated by approximately 302 feet, which would satisfy the 300-foot separation requirement typically applied to freestanding monument signs within commercial centers.


However, the primary issue does not appear to be the separation distance itself. The larger consideration is whether the site's PAD zoning and any previously approved sign package or Master Sign Program would permit the additional monument sign arrangement. The Chandler Sign Code indicates that PAD developments may be governed by previously approved sign criteria that can supersede the standard code provisions.


Because of this, I would not consider the layout automatically approved based solely on the Sign Code. The proposal appears supportable from a spacing standpoint, but final determination should come from the Planning Department after reviewing the parcel configuration, ownership structure, PAD approvals, and existing sign program for the site.


My recommendation is that we contact Chandler Planning and request confirmation that the proposed arrangement of a separate Chick-fil-A monument sign and a separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign would be acceptable under the current PAD approvals.


Please let me know if you would like me to reach out to the city and obtain their interpretation.

subject: Alma Parks (SGN26-0139) – Property Manager Authorization Requirement (06/23/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I have submittal the application for Alma Parks (Permit Application No. SGN26-0139) and reviewed the City of Chandler's document requirements.


The City lists several items including property manager authorization, sign details, engineering, footing details, and a site plan. Based on my review, we have already addressed most of these requirements through the artwork package and site map being uploaded with the application.


The one item I do not currently have is documentation of Property Manager / Property Owner authorization. Chandler specifically notes that this can be provided in several forms, including:

• Letter from the Property Manager or Property Owner
• Contractor authorization form signed by the Property Manager or Property Owner
• Sign drawings signed by the Property Manager or Property Owner


Currently, I recommend that we focus on obtaining the authorization letter and proceed with the submittal. The remaining items appear to be covered by the artwork package and supporting documents already prepared for the project.


Please let me know if you have an existing authorization letter or a contact at the property management company who can provide one.


Best,

 

Steve Skye

subject: White Castle Arizona Sign Expansion Research Update (06/26/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I wanted to provide you with a quick update on the White Castle sign expansion research.


We have made significant progress with the SRPMIC (The Block) and Goodyear locations by obtaining and reviewing the approved sign packages, permit records, and applicable Comprehensive Sign Plans.



Current findings:

*	SRPMIC (The Block): Our comparison indicates approximately 68.35 sq. ft. of potential additional wall sign area may be available. Any proposed revisions would first require review and approval by MainSpring Capital Group (master lessee) before being submitted to the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community for permitting.
*	Goodyear: Based on the approved permit package and the Market at Estrella Falls Comprehensive Sign Plan, approximately 38.75 sq. ft. of additional sign area appears to remain available.
*	Tempe: We have spoken with the City and have a good understanding of the approval process. While we have not yet quantified the available sign area, we believe there may be additional capacity beyond the currently approved signage.


Although both the SRPMIC and Goodyear locations appear to have some remaining sign area available, these are relatively small square footage increases. Pursuing any changes will require careful design work and coordination with the applicable property managers, landlords, and permitting authorities, and there is no guarantee that additional signage will ultimately be approved.


Please let me know if needing any additional assistance.

subject: Findings from Roof Investigation – Fast Auto Title Loans (06/29/26)
body:
Hi Martin,



Thank you for allowing Christy Signs the opportunity to investigate the reported electrical shock condition at your Fast Auto Title Loans location.


Our technician completed a thorough inspection of the existing building sign, its electrical components, and the surrounding rooftop conditions. Based on our findings, we did not identify any electrical faults, damaged wiring, or hazardous conditions associated with the sign or its electrical system.


The condition appears to be the result of static electricity generated by the recently coated synthetic roofing surface. As personnel walk across the roof, friction between their footwear and the roof membrane can create an electrostatic charge. That charge is then discharged when a grounded metal object—such as rooftop equipment, flashing, or other metal components—is touched.


This type of static buildup is common on newer synthetic roofing systems, particularly during hot, dry, low-humidity conditions such as those we experience in the Phoenix area.

Based on our inspection, we do not believe the sign installation is the source of the reported shocks, and no repairs to the sign are recommended at this time.


If the static condition continues to be a concern, we recommend consulting the roofing contractor or roofing manufacturer to verify the roofing material and discuss possible anti-static treatments or other mitigation options that are compatible with the roofing system.


Please let me know if you have any questions regarding our findings or if we can be of any further assistance.


Thank you,

 

Steve Skye

subject: Findings from Roof Investigation – Fast Auto Title Loans (06/29/26)
body:
Hi Martin,



Thank you for allowing Christy Signs the opportunity to investigate the reported electrical shock condition at your Fast Auto Title Loans location.


Our technician completed a thorough inspection of the existing building sign, its electrical components, and the surrounding rooftop conditions. Based on our findings, we did not identify any electrical faults, damaged wiring, or hazardous conditions associated with the sign or its electrical system.


The condition appears to be the result of static electricity generated by the recently coated synthetic roofing surface. As personnel walk across the roof, friction between their footwear and the roof membrane can create an electrostatic charge. That charge is then discharged when a grounded metal object—such as rooftop equipment, flashing, or other metal components—is touched.


This type of static buildup is common on newer synthetic roofing systems, particularly during hot, dry, low-humidity conditions such as those we experience in the Phoenix area.

Based on our inspection, we do not believe the sign installation is the source of the reported shocks, and no repairs to the sign are recommended at this time.


If the static condition continues to be a concern, we recommend consulting the roofing contractor or roofing manufacturer to verify the roofing material and discuss possible anti-static treatments or other mitigation options that are compatible with the roofing system.


Please let me know if you have any questions regarding our findings or if we can be of any further assistance.


Thank you,

subject: FW: Alma Park (WO 26636) – Chandler Plan Review Corrections (07/01/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



The City of Chandler has completed the first review of the Alma Park sign permit application and has issued correction comments. Overall, the comments are straightforward and primarily require revisions to the drawings rather than redesign of the signs.


The city is requesting the following updates before the application can be resubmitted:



*	Engineering: Provide sealed structural details for each monument sign prepared by a Structural or Civil Engineer. We can use the ASA engineering worksheet if desired. 
*	Electrical Information: Expand the electrical notes to fully comply with 2024 IBC / 2023 NEC Article 600. The plans should identify: 

	*	Source electrical panel and panel designation. 
	*	Dedicated 120V, 20A branch circuit. 
	*	Conductor type and size. 
	*	Conduit type, size, and burial depth. 
	*	External lockable disconnect switch located within sight of the sign. 
	*	Equipment grounding and bonding per NEC Article 600. 
	*	UL-listed sign components and installation in accordance with NEC Article 600 and local electrical codes. 

*	Tenant Panel Construction: Revise the specifications to state that all illuminated tenant panels are routed with 1/2-inch push-thru acrylic rather than "back-up acrylic." All three monument signs should use identical construction terminology and matching fabrication criteria.
*	Panel Color: Note the background color for the tenant panels and indicate that all tenant panels will have matching background colors
*	Site Plan: Provide a revised site detail showing: 

	*	Exact monument sign location. 
	*	Setback from the back of curb. 
	*	Distances to the nearest property lines and right-of-way. 
	*	Required visibility triangles demonstrating the sign does not obstruct vehicular sight distance. 
		
		

This shopping center may have a Comprehensive Sign Program (CSP), I have called the City of Chandler sign department to check if this is the case. 


Once these revisions are completed, we can upload the revised plans for the next review cycle.


Regards,

subject: Stotz Equipment #074063 – Survey Exhibit Request (07/02/26)
body:
Hi Casey / Chris,



Chris,
Thank you for the prompt turnaround on the Right-of-Way Exhibit. This is exactly what we needed to establish the controlling property and right-of-way dimensions for the project.


I do have one question before we move forward. The County's review comments also reference identifying all easements associated with the property (Schedule B easements) and documenting that they do not conflict with the proposed sign location. Can you please confirm whether your exhibit satisfies that portion of the review, or if additional easement information would need to be incorporated?


If no additional work is required, I believe that will conclude your portion of the project.


Casey,

Now that we have the controlling property and right-of-way dimensions established, the next step will be determining where Pattison ID and John Deere would like the monument sign to be located within the area available for construction.

subject: Stotz Equipment #074063 – Revised Construction Drawings Submitted (07/07/26)
body:
Hi Casey,



I wanted to let you know that we have completed our response to the Maricopa County review comments and submitted the revised construction drawing package for the Stotz Equipment project. The updated drawing set includes the revisions discussed during our coordination meeting, including the separation of the Building Plan Set and Site Plan Set, as well as the addition of the stamped Right-of-Way Exhibit. 


Our response addresses the County's comments by:

*	Separating the Building Plan Set from the Site Plan Set in accordance with County review procedures. 
*	Including the stamped Right-of-Way Exhibit prepared by OGI Land Surveyors. 
*	Revising the Site Plan to reflect the MCDOT future right-of-way requirements and the required 25-foot setback from the east property line. 
*	Providing written responses to each outstanding review comment as part of the resubmittal package. 


The revised plans have now been submitted for the County's review. We'll continue to monitor the review process and keep you informed of any additional comments or the permit approval status.


Please let me know if you have any questions or if you need copies of any of the submitted documents.

Hi Wendy,



Thank you for your feedback.


It is understood by everyone involved that the roof-mounted option is most likely not approvable under the City's sign regulations. The concept wasn't developed because we expect it to be approved; rather, it came directly from our onsite meeting with both the property owner and the DiMaggio's ownership. They asked us to illustrate the concept so they could determine whether they wanted to pursue it, understanding it would be a long shot.


Rocky is aware of the direction we're taking, and everything remains in the conceptual stage. Before anything is presented to the customer, I'll make it very clear in writing that the roof-mounted concept is nonconforming and highly unlikely to receive City approval. If they choose to pursue it, it would only be with that understanding.


I also agree that the wall sign should be the primary focus. I like your suggestion of enhancing it—possibly with a halo-lit back panel or other features (the property owner liked that idea too) —to create a stronger focal point while remaining within what is much more likely to be approved.


We've developed a very positive relationship with both the property owner and the DiMaggio's team, and I believe we're very close to finalizing the agreement, hopefully sometime next week.


Thanks,

 

Steve Skye

subject: Proposed Plan for PSCO / ID Associates Payment Terms (07/13/26)
body:
Hi Wendy,



Following your email concerning adjusting the terms for PSCO / ID Associates, I spoke with Pat Chevrette, their A/P Manager for better understand how they handle payment arrangements.


Pat explained that they are willing to work with vendors on payment terms, but these discussions are typically handled with the project manager before the purchase order is issued. Depending on the project, they can accommodate:

*	Net 30 terms (when approved) 
*	Deposits 
*	Upfront payment of permit fees 
*	Upfront payment of crane or other significant third-party costs 
*	Progress payments on larger projects 


Based on that conversation, here is my proposed plan:



Aaron's and Tractor Supply (Current Projects)

I will contact each project manager and request a progress payment to reimburse Christy Signs for costs already incurred, including permit fees and other project-related expenses. Pat explained that the project managers have the authority to approve special payment arrangements, and if they approve an interim payment, she will coordinate the payment through Accounts Payable.

If the project managers prefer to leave the existing payment terms unchanged, we will continue following their established A/P process by sending invoices directly to Pat and monitoring payment through completion.



Darr Equipment (Future Purchase Order)

Since the purchase order has not yet been issued, this is the appropriate time to discuss payment terms with the project manager before the PO is released. I will explain that Christy Signs would like to establish payment terms that work well for both companies and discuss options such as a deposit, progress payments, upfront payment of permit fees, crane costs, or other significant project expenses before the purchase order is finalized.

 

Going forward, I recommend that we make this part of our standard process for PSCO / ID Associates. Rather than automatically accepting their default 45-day terms, we should discuss and establish payment terms with the project manager before each purchase order is issued. This will help manage Christy Signs' credit exposure while maintaining a positive working relationship with the customer.


Please let me know if you would like me to modify this approach before I begin contacting the project managers.


Thank you,

 

Steve Skye

subject: Bodybar – Final Inspection Requirements (07/14/26)
body:
Hi Scott,



I spoke with the City of Avondale Inspection Department regarding the final inspection requirements.


They confirmed that the sign may be installed before permanent power is available. However, the final inspection cannot be called in until the primary electrical wiring from a dedicated circuit has been installed and connected to the sign.


Once the dedicated circuit is in place and the sign is connected, we can schedule the final inspection with the city.

subject: Illuminated Bollard Project – Follow-Up (07/14/26)
body:
Hi Jon and Tyler,



Thank you again for taking the time to meet with us to discuss the illuminated bollard project.


We appreciated the opportunity to review the concept and were encouraged by the discussion surrounding the internal LED lighting approach. My understanding was that the concept of using an internal LED light stick to illuminate the laser-cut logo and lettering was well received. Since the site lighting at the base of the bollards may not yet be installed, this interior illumination method appears to be a practical alternative for achieving the desired effect.


I wanted to check in to see if the revised design is available so we can finalize our pricing for the project. If the revised artwork is ready, please send it over and we'll update our proposal accordingly.

subject: U-Haul Maricopa – Comprehensive Sign Plan Review Summary (07/15/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,


The Town of Maricopa has completed its first review of the proposed Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP). The comments primarily focus on reducing the amount of signage proposed, modifying illumination adjacent to residential uses, and improving the monument sign design.


Below is a summary of the review comments and the applicable code provisions.



1. Aggregate Sign Area

The reviewer determined that the proposed sign package is significantly larger than can be approved.

The review notes that the total aggregate signage proposed cannot exceed 150% of the aggregate signage otherwise permitted by the zoning code, and further states that the maximum aggregate sign area for each building on separate lots is 150 square feet.

I reviewed the Maricopa Sign Ordinance and was unable to locate the 150% limitation within Chapter 18.115. The ordinance establishes the base sign allowances for commercial properties and allows Comprehensive Sign Plans to deviate from those standards when justified through superior architectural integration and design, but it does not expressly state a 150% cap. This appears to be an administrative policy or interpretation being applied by the Planning Department rather than language contained directly within the ordinance.


2. North Elevation Illumination

The reviewer notes that all illuminated signage facing Honeycutt Road must be revised.

This comment is supported directly by Maricopa City Code §18.115.070(F), which states:

"Signs directly facing residential districts shall not be illuminated."

Since the north elevations face the residential neighborhood across Honeycutt Road, those cabinet signs will need to be converted to non-illuminated versions.


3. Monument Sign

The reviewer is requesting that the proposed monument sign receive greater architectural treatment, specifically enhancing both the monument base and the sign structure itself.

The review also reminds us that monument sign height is measured from grade. Under §18.115.090(C), freestanding monument signs in commercial districts are limited to 6 feet in height, and §18.115.060(B)(1) specifies that height is measured from the adjacent curb or street grade to the highest point of the sign, including the monument base.

The ordinance also indicates that Comprehensive Sign Plans should promote superior architectural integration with the site and surrounding development, which appears to be the basis for the request to provide additional architectural interest.


4. Remaining Plan Sheets

The comments on the individual building elevations (Pages 6 through 10 and Page 12) simply reference the primary comments above and request that the plans be revised accordingly. No additional project-specific comments were provided for those sheets.


5. Property Owner Authorization

The Property Owner Approval Letter will need to be revised to include the printed name and title of the individual signing the authorization.


My recommendation would be to schedule a meeting with Derek (the reviewer) before revising the plans. Several comments are clear and can be addressed directly; however, the overall sign area comments appear to rely on an administrative interpretation of the Comprehensive Sign Plan provisions rather than an explicit code requirement. A short meeting should help us confirm the City's expectations, avoid unnecessary redesign, and improve the likelihood of approval on the next submittal.


Best,

 

Steve Skye

Subject: RE: Coral Gables Estates – Preliminary Site Review Report (07/15/26)

 

We do not have any drawing or renderings at this time, we are working on getting bids for the below items.           

Windows: replace all 3 sets of windows with new Vinyl framed glass, frames should be black or dark bronze inside and out, glass should be E90 tint or better, glass panels should slide side to side to open (not up and down), bug screens should be included, labor and installation should be included, list warranties on glass/frames/installation

 

Doors: replace both exterior doors with commercial grade glass doors with slim metal frames, frames should be black or dark bronze inside and out, door opening system that holds door open on a locked position with a pull close system, include insulated strips and door sweeps for complete fit

 

Exterior Stucco - a traditional ‘Santa Barbara flat finish’ on all exterior surfaces except for soffits.  Complete wall to wall, floor to ceiling coverage including wrapping corners and base of walls.  

 

Interior - remove interior door, frame and drywall leading to the back room (where the refrigerator is now) and remove existing decorative window in that back room, frame it out with drywall and stucco.  This will create one large continuous wall area for all of the mailboxes.  Move existing mailboxes to this area.  

 

Interior walls - new ‘flat smooth finish’ on top of all existing drywall (walls and ceiling), fully sanded to final ‘ready to paint’ finish

 

Interior flooring - remove toilet, remove all existing flooring down to smooth concrete subfloor, remove all existing baseboards, replace with ‘through body porcelain’ tiles size 24 x 24 or 24 x 28 and all new baseboards that have been primed. Install new standard size (elongated bowl and seat) white Kohler toilet.  Tile color and design TBD but should be in the family of Grey.

 

Cabinets - sand existing cabinets to base wood, either stain or paint cabinets (color TBD) and seal them.  Do not remove cabinets nor countertops.  

 

Interior lighting - remove both existing fluorescent light fixtures and replace with white Can lighting and LED daylight white bulbs, install 4 or 5 blade new ceiling fan, dark bronze or black  (hugging the ceiling, no drop rod) in the middle of the space. Basic fan such as Hunter or similar brand with a wall remote.

 

Roof - remove all existing tile.  Get quotes for 2 different options: 

1. Standing seam metal in matte black or dark bronze.  Add matching metal fascia for a finished look.

2. Flat profile concrete tile in dark charcoal or black. Add wood fascia for finished look. Check existing felt to ensure useful life. 

 

Exterior signs - remove existing wooden community name sign and ‘Stop’ sign.  Replace community sign with decorative metal script sign and replace stop sign with basic metal sign // suggested design formats welcome, should be modern with matte black or dark bronze lettering to compliment metal or flat profile roof and possibly with back lighting for the community name sign.

 

Paint - all exterior walls: white primer, white Sherwin Williams paint with semi-gloss finish.  Exterior columns: gray primer, matte black paint Sherwin Williams eggshell finish.  All Interior walls and ceiling: white primer white Sherwin Williams paint with satin finish.

body:
Hi Derek,



Thank you again for discussing the U-Haul Maricopa CSP with me. Before we revise the artwork, could you please confirm whether our attached summary correctly applies the sign-area allowance?


Using the 154-foot frontage shown on the elevations:

*	154 LF × 0.75 SF/LF = 115.50 SF
*	115.50 SF × 150% = 173.25 SF


Should this result be capped at 150 SF per building, or is the 150 SF maximum applied separately to each elevation?


We currently understand the allowance to be 150 SF aggregate per building—300 SF total for the UMSC and U-Box buildings—with each building’s allowance distributable among its elevations.

subject: Crossroads Tower Sign (Formerly Hayden Professional Center) – PA-0470-2026 (07/24/26)
body:
Hi Andrew,



I hope you're doing well.


We're beginning to develop the proposed sign package for the Crossroads Tower Sign project (formerly Hayden Professional Center) under Pre-Application PA-0470-2026, and we have a design question that wasn't discussed during our pre-application meeting.


We're considering proposing the Crossroads identification as individual channel letters mounted to a ½-inch painted wireway, with the wireway color-matched to the surrounding brick to minimize its visibility.


The intent is to preserve the historic character of the building by minimizing penetrations into the existing brick façade. A color-matched painted wireway would be largely concealed while significantly reducing the number of mounting and wiring holes required for individually mounted letters.


Would this type of proposal be appropriate for another design review meeting? We'd appreciate the opportunity for a brief phone call to explain the concept and get your initial thoughts before moving further with the design.


Please let me know if you have a few minutes to discuss it at your convenience.


Thank you, and I look forward to hearing from you.


Warmest Regards,

 

Steve Skye

Subject: Chandler Review Corrections – Chick-fil-A #2567 (04/13/26)

 

Hi Scott,

I wanted to bring to your attention the review comments issued by the City of Chandler Sign Department for the Chick-fil-A #2567 project (SGN26-0083).


The City has completed their initial review and provided corrections that will need to be addressed prior to permit approval.


At a high level:

• The site plan currently reflects a proposed layout that has not yet been approved by Planning. Because of this, the reviewer cannot approve the plan as submitted.
• The reviewer has marked certain ground signs to be omitted for now. They are requesting that we revise the plan set and resubmit without those signs so that the wall signs and remaining signage can be approved.
• Once Planning approves the overall site layout, a subsequent submittal will be required for the omitted ground signs.


Additionally:

• All drive-thru directional signs must be reduced to a maximum height of 3'-0" (36").
• Future resubmittals must clearly show all directional sign locations and confirm compliance with this height requirement.


In summary, we can proceed by revising the current plan set to remove the flagged signs and move forward with approval of the wall signage, while the ground signs will follow after Planning finalizes the site plan.


I’ve attached the full correction set for your review. Let me know how you’d like to proceed, and we can begin coordinating the revisions.


Best regards,

Steve Skye

From: Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com> 
Sent: Friday, June 5, 2026 12:43 PM
To: Taylor Wenzel <twenzel@everbrite.com>
Cc: Scott Frazer <scott@christysigns.com>
Subject: Habit Burger # 65027 (27782) – Glendale Correction Comments (06/05/26)

 



 

Hi Taylor,




Attached are the City of Glendale correction comments and redlined plans for the Habit Burger project.


Please review and revise the drawings accordingly. The primary comments are summarized below:




Planning Comments

1. Property Line / Right-of-Way

*        The property line must be clearly shown on the site plan.

*        The city notes that no signs may be located within the public right-of-way.

2. Building Sign Area

*        The city has determined that the building sign allowance is based on the available business frontage.

*        The submitted building sign is shown at approximately 26.62 square feet, while the reviewer indicates an allowable area of approximately 16.4 square feet based on the frontage shown.

*        Please review and revise the sign size or provide any supporting information necessary to demonstrate compliance.

3. Drive-Thru Sign Height

*        The city requires the exact height from finished grade to the top of the drive-thru sign.

*        Per Glendale Code Section 35.4.310(E)(2)(b), drive-thru signs are limited to 64 square feet in area and 6 feet in height.

*        The reviewer has requested that the sign height be reduced to comply with the ordinance.




Structural Comments

4. Arizona-Sealed Engineering

*        The city is requiring drawings and calculations sealed by an Arizona-registered engineer for the overhead sign structures and associated foundations.

5. Foundation Coordination

*        Several foundation details require clarification.

*        The reviewer noted that certain dimensions do not match between sheets and that some foundation details are not clearly associated with a specific sign.

*        Please coordinate the foundation drawings and clearly identify which sign each foundation detail applies to.

6. Structural Information

*        Additional column, frame, foundation, and connection information is required for review and approval.


Please provide revised drawings, Arizona-sealed engineering (as required), and a written response letter addressing each comment so we can prepare the resubmittal package.


Let me know if you have any questions regarding the City's comments.


Thank you,

Steve, Rocky,

 

In case we don’t talk today, here is the summary.

 

Planning has been approached by all parties for this signage proposal, and they have stated several times that no individual tenant signage will be considered, only the multi-tenant signs that match the new remodeled versions (8’ max height).

 

We can approve 2 new multi-tenant signs in that span. Starting from the larger 14’ sign in between the carwash and Wendy’s, and moving west, we can do a new sign every 275’ (min), as there is exactly room for 2.

 

These signs must be approved and permitted as duplicates of the existing signs, BUT…..The tenant panels can be manipulated per the discretion of the PM to accommodate individual tenants requests. For example, the sign must be approved with 5 max panels per side, but if the PM wanted to allow one tenant, usually like a major or anchor tenant, to utilize the space or total area of 2 or 3 panels, then they can allow this. So then you would have the same sign and sign panel area but with one large panel and 2 smaller ones. Just an example. The only requirements are that the panel background colors must meet the sign criteria (white), no corporate-colored panels, only corporate colored copy and graphics…ROUTED AND PUSH-THRU.

 

I hope this makes sense! Except for being away from my desk occasionally, I am here until 4:50 today and back in tomorrow at 8am.

 

Thank you!

 

Joe Sauer

We are looking for some guidance regarding a proposed monument sign arrangement within the Desert Palms development at Alma School Road and Warner Road.

While this appears to satisfy the typical monument sign separation requirement, we are unsure whether the site's PAD zoning, Master Sign Program, or previously approved sign package would permit this arrangement.

Hi Rocky,

I reviewed the Chandler Sign Code along with the site plan provided.


Based on the plan, the proposed Chick-fil-A monument sign and the AZP multi-tenant monument sign appear to be separated by approximately 302 feet, which would satisfy the 300-foot separation requirement typically applied to freestanding monument signs within commercial centers.


However, the primary issue does not appear to be the separation distance itself. The larger consideration is whether the site's PAD zoning and any previously approved sign package or Master Sign Program would permit the additional monument sign arrangement. The Chandler Sign Code indicates that PAD developments may be governed by previously approved sign criteria that can supersede the standard code provisions.


Because of this, I would not consider the layout automatically approved based solely on the Sign Code. The proposal appears supportable from a spacing standpoint, but final determination should come from the Planning Department after reviewing the parcel configuration, ownership structure, PAD approvals, and existing sign program for the site.


My recommendation is that we contact Chandler Planning and request confirmation that the proposed arrangement of a separate Chick-fil-A monument sign and a separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign would be acceptable under the current PAD approvals.


Please let me know if you would like me to reach out to the city and obtain their interpretation.

Hi Joe,

We are looking for some guidance regarding a proposed monument sign arrangement within the Desert Palms development at Alma School Road and Warner Road.


Attached is a site plan showing the proposed locations of:

• One Chick-fil-A monument sign
• One AZP multi-tenant monument sign


Based on the plan, the two proposed signs appear to be separated by approximately 302 feet. While this appears to satisfy the typical monument sign separation requirement, we are unsure whether the site's PAD zoning, Master Sign Program, or previously approved sign package would permit this arrangement.

A separate Chick-fil-A monument sign and a separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign located approximately 302 feet apart within the same overall development.

Hi Rocky,

I reviewed the Chandler Sign Code along with the site plan provided.


Based on the plan, the proposed Chick-fil-A monument sign and the AZP multi-tenant monument sign appear to be separated by approximately 302 feet, which would satisfy the 300-foot separation requirement typically applied to freestanding monument signs within commercial centers.


However, the primary issue does not appear to be the separation distance itself. The larger consideration is whether the site's PAD zoning and any previously approved sign package or Master Sign Program would permit the additional monument sign arrangement. The Chandler Sign Code indicates that PAD developments may be governed by previously approved sign criteria that can supersede the standard code provisions.


Because of this, I would not consider the layout automatically approved based solely on the Sign Code. The proposal appears supportable from a spacing standpoint, but final determination should come from the Planning Department after reviewing the parcel configuration, ownership structure, PAD approvals, and existing sign program for the site.


My recommendation is that we contact Chandler Planning and request confirmation that the proposed arrangement of a separate Chick-fil-A monument sign and a separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign would be acceptable under the current PAD approvals.


Please let me know if you would like me to reach out to the city and obtain their interpretation.

Hello Steve,

We’re updating our settings to give you even more control over saved history and personalized recommendations across Google Search services, including Search, Maps, Shopping, Hotels, Flights, Translate, and News. You’ll see this change in your Google Account in the next few days.

What’s changing

Previously, saving history and personalization were managed by Web & App Activity. Going forward, we're introducing two new settings to help you better tailor your experience: Search Services History and Personalized Recommendations. These settings let you revisit your past searches and decide if you want your experience to be personalized. You can turn these settings on or off at any time. As people increasingly search in new ways, like searching a photo with Lens, Search Services History now includes media from your interactions, which you can stop saving at any time. 

How this affects your account

*	New history and personalization settings: These new settings will reflect your most recent choices for Web & App Activity and Search Personalization settings. If these are currently on, these new settings will stay on. If they’re off, the new settings will be off. After the transition, Web & App Activity and Search services settings will be separate, and changes to one won’t affect the other.
*	Auto-delete: Your prior choice from Web & App Activity for how long your history is saved will also apply to Search Services History. As always, you can change how long history is saved, choose an auto-delete period, and review or delete history manually at any time.
*	Your media is saved when Search Services History is on: Saved media includes your images, files, audio and video from your interactions with Search services to help improve your experience. For example, this lets you revisit your past visual searches with Lens or continue a Search Live conversation about a song you heard. To support these types of interactive product experiences, Google will now save your media to your Search Services History, applying robust privacy and security protections. Like your Search Services History, your saved media is also used to develop and improve Google services and technologies, including AI models and safety measures. With this transition, if your Web & App Activity setting is currently turned on, this new Save Media subsetting will also be turned on along with your Search Services History. Good morning, Kevin,



Thank you for your email.



I have attached the production artwork along with current site photos showing the existing damaged primary power feed located behind the wall where the new Bel Fleur sign will be connected. The artwork shows the sign layout and electrical connection details for reference.



The primary power serving the previous sign was most likely a standard 120-volt circuit utilizing 12-gauge solid copper conductors on a dedicated 20-amp breaker. This is typically what we would expect for this type of illuminated reverse channel letter installation.


Our installation team will make the final sign connection and complete all wiring within the sign assembly. We would simply ask that the dedicated 120-volt power feed be brought to the existing connection location behind the wall and left accessible for our installers.


The attached photos show the current condition of the existing electrical components and conduit. Based on what we observed, it appears there was previously power serving a sign at this location.

	I’m inquiring about banners for a pickleball fundraising tournament we’re holding in the fall. I am with Home Fur Good, a non-profit animal rescue organization located in Phoenix. Per our phone call yesterday, here are the details of the banners:

	Quantity: 12
	Size: 5’ x 3’
	Material: vinyl
	Each banner will be different (name and logo of each company sponsoring the event + Home Fur Good’s logo).
	Event location:: indoors (no wind slit needed), will need grommets for hanging.
	Date of event:  Nov. 7, 2026
	 
	Please provide the following information:

	1. Quote for 12 banners, including tax.
	2. If a specific file type and/or size is needed.
	3. Minimum lead-time you would need for printing.
	4. If a discount is available for non-profits.
	5. Is there a min. deposit amount required to place an order?
	6. Anything else you think is pertinent for us to be aware of. 

	Thank you for your assistance!

	Karen Stovall
