Hello All,

I am writing regarding the subject property and the recently installed EMC sign.

The Town has already begun receiving complaints regarding the excessive brightness and glare from the sign. I understand the lighting is controlled by sensors and that the intensity can be adjusted.. however, it is unclear who is responsible for monitoring and making those adjustments..

At this time, please provide a written response outlining what steps have been taken, or will be taken, to address the brightness concerns and bring the sign into compliance with the intent of the Council’s CUP approval. Please also include the anticipated timeframe for any adjustments.

If the concerns continue or if the Town is unable to confirm that appropriate adjustments are being made, staff may need to request additional documentation, including a photometric plan, to further evaluate the sign’s impact.

Your prompt response is appreciated so we can demonstrate that the matter is being addressed and avoid the need for further investigation.

Ticket Status Notification

Ticket Information

33.3813902080138, -111.9631597451 

Due Date: 06/04/2026 8:00 PM ET

Company: CHRISTY SIGNS

Phone: 6022424488

Fax/Email:  / STEVE@CHRISTYSIGNS.COM

 




Reason for Notification

Notification Type: Bore Standby        Date: 06/02/2026

You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path. 

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations. 

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a 

minimum of 2 hours prior. 

 480-730-3640

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path. 

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations. 

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a 

minimum of 2 hours prior. 

 480-730-3640

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.

Subject: [EXT]: Chandler Fashion Center – Freeway Pylon Sign Proposal (05/29/26)

 

Hi Andy and Monica,

Happy Friday!


Thank you again for the opportunity to earn your business and to present our proposal for the future freeway identification sign at Chandler Fashion Center.


Attached please find our proposal and updated concept artwork for your review. The design reflects the revisions discussed and presents a new 75-foot freeway pylon sign intended to enhance visibility for Chandler Fashion Center and its major tenants. The proposed sign incorporates an illuminated center identification element along with multiple tenant panel locations that can be updated as tenant needs evolve.


Our goal was to develop a sign that is visually impactful from the freeway while remaining consistent with the quality, character, and scale of the center.


We appreciate the opportunity to be considered for this project and look forward to discussing the proposal with you. If you have any questions, comments, or would like to review alternative options, please do not hesitate to contact us.


Thank you again for your time, consideration, and the opportunity to work with Chandler Fashion Center. We look forward to your feedback.


Warm regards,

Here are the direct answers to your questions:


Building Sign Area (Major vs. Minor Tenants)
    • Glendale's sign code does not establish separate square footage allowances for "major tenants" versus "minor tenants."
    • Building sign area is generally calculated based on each tenant's linear frontage and applicable building sign standards contained in Section 35.4.311.


Number of Signs Per Elevation
    • The code does not appear to limit a tenant to only one sign per elevation.
    • The focus is on the total allowable sign area rather than a specific number of wall signs.


Four-Sided Pad Buildings
    • Yes, pad buildings are generally allowed signage on multiple sides.
    • Elevations facing public streets, drive aisles, and prominent customer-facing areas are typically eligible for signage.
    • The allowable square footage is determined based on the qualifying frontage and applicable code provisions.


Recommendation
    • I recommend we follow the same approach used in the City's approved 303 & Bethany Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) example.
    • That CSP does not establish detailed major-tenant/minor-tenant wall sign standards. Instead, it states that all building-mounted signs will be reviewed and approved under the standard City of Glendale Sign Ordinance.
    • This keeps the CSP clean and allows future tenant signage to be reviewed under the City's current code requirements.

Hi Rocky,

I reviewed the Glendale Sign Ordinance, the Stonehaven PAD documents, and the available site information for Stonehaven Marketplace (NEC 91st Avenue & Camelback Road).


A few key findings:

• The site is zoned PAD (Planned Area Development) and the Stonehaven PAD specifically references preparation of a Commercial Master Sign Plan (CMSP) for the commercial portion of the development (see attached).

• The Glendale Sign Ordinance establishes the overall sign limitations such as sign type, height, area, and quantity, but it does not appear to establish major tenant versus minor tenant panel standards or tenant hierarchy requirements.


Based on the Glendale Sign Ordinance:


Freestanding Monument Signs
• One monument sign is permitted per 200 linear feet of street frontage.
• The site has approximately:

*         995.9 LF along Camelback Road

*         890.4 LF along 91st Avenue
• Based on frontage, the site could support up to three monument signs per frontage (six total), although the current concept showing two monument signs per frontage (four total) appears to be a more practical and defensible approach.
• Maximum height: 14 feet.
• Maximum sign area: 110 square feet per sign (parcel exceeds 20 acres).


Directional Signs
• Directional signs are permitted.
• Maximum size: 6 square feet.
• Maximum height: 3 feet.
• The code does not appear to establish a maximum number of directional signs, but they should be limited to legitimate traffic circulation and wayfinding purposes.


Tenant Panels / Major vs. Minor Tenants
I have not found any code section that specifically establishes:
• Number of tenant panels per monument sign.
• Major tenant versus minor tenant classifications.
• Required panel sizes.
• Required tenant hierarchy.
• Tenant copy size requirements.
• Anchor tenant panel requirements.


My interpretation is that these standards are intended to be created through the Commercial Master Sign Plan itself. In other words, Glendale provides the overall monument sign envelope (quantity, height, and area), while the CMSP establishes how the tenant panels are organized and displayed.


For the narrative, I would recommend establishing:
• Major Tenant panel standards.
• Minor Tenant panel standards.
• Tenant panel sizing criteria.
• Tenant hierarchy and placement standards.
• Directional sign program.
• Consistent monument sign design standards for the center.


I have attached the research summary and supporting code analysis for reference.


Best,

Re: U-Haul Sahuarita – Proposed Comprehensive Sign Plan Review (05/28/26)
body:
Steve,

I did a quick review of what you submitted. The amount of signage you are proposing would not be allowed even with an approved CSP. The CSP allows for up to a 20% increase in sign area with Planning & Zoning Commission approval. The South elevation is currently proposing over a 100% increase from the 225 sq. feet maximum allowed. There are other elevations that also exceed what would be allowed with a CSP. Based on the proposed signs your CSP application would most likely not qualify for all of the elements that contribute to the allowable 20% increase. I would recommend reviewing the 4 criteria that provide 5% increases.
I realize that this was not a complete submittal but also wanted to give you a heads up that your application materials need to provide items F, G and H from the required elements in the code, also listed below.


*	
	Total proposed sign area per frontage, per sign type, and overall for the project.




*	
	Maximum allowed sign area per frontage, per sign type, and overall for the project, and explanations of how the maximums were calculated.




*	
	If the applicant proposes a deviation from the standards set forth in this chapter, the following additional information shall be provided:

    

*	
	A detailed explanation of the deviations being proposed.




*	
	A written justification for the deviations.



If you have any questions, please contact Orlanthia as I will be on vacation for a few weeks.

Thanks,
Dylan

Hi Kristi, 

Thank you again for being part of the conference call with Bill Peckinpaugh  from the City of Surprise  concerning the current review comments for the Tractor Supply Co – Surprise (#2479)  permit application. 


Based on the discussion with Bill, the remaining electrical comment appears to primarily concern standard NEC Article 600 compliance information  associated with the illuminated storefront channel letters shown on Page 2  of the package. 


The city is generally looking for clarification concerning the following items: 

*	*    Dedicated power source / branch circuit  feeding the illuminated sign 
*	*    Disconnect switch location  for the storefront channel letters 
*	*    Confirmation that the disconnect is located “within sight of” the sign per NEC 600.6(A) 

 


Bill indicated that the electrical corrections needed provide standard clarification notes and disconnect identification associated with the illuminated sign installation. 


For practical purposes, the revisions on Page 2  would likely include: 

*	*    Adding the project address  to the drawing sheets 
*	*    Adding a disconnect location callout  to the storefront elevation 
*	*    Adding NEC Article 600 compliance notes 
*	*    Clarifying sign power supply / circuit information 

 


The storefront elevation and mounting details already included within the exhibit package should substantially assist in satisfying the Architectural  and Structural  review comments as well. 


Please let me know if needed any additional assistance in preparing the formal resubmittal package. 


Best regards,

subject: Re: Chandler Fashion Center – Engineering / Structural Feasibility Questions (05/28/26)
body:
Greetings!

Thank you again for the request and opportunity. Please find our estimate in the body of this email for expediency in processing this service request.

To award and move forward, please simply reply as such and we will do the rest. If your standard process is to issue PO, please provide the document or number at the time of the award.
 
If you require expedited or guaranteed services compared to our offering below, please let us know immediately and we will provide some options for you as quickly as possible.


~~~~~~~~~~ BEGIN INFORMAL ESTIMATE ~~~~~~~~~~

PROJECT: 2605070 - Chandler Fashion Center Pylon Sign - Chandler, AZ
 
SCOPE OF WORK:
1. Preliminary Engineering for 75' Pylon on Sheet 1 (cast-in-place pier foundation & primary support pole only, does not include stamped engineering): $270 

SUBTOTAL: $270.00

SHIPPING: None at this time 

ESTIMATED DELIVERY SCHEDULE: approximately 2-3 business days after award.


~~~~~~~~~~ END INFORMAL ESTIMATE ~~~~~~~~~~
 
For your consideration, please find below our General Service Understandings:
 
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
General Service Understandings  ← Updated January 2024: please familiarize yourself!
1. The base deliverable is a digital set of structural drawings (11x17) and an accompanying set of structural calculations (8.5x11) produced by Reverence Engineering unless communicated otherwise.
2. The base deliverable will be stamped and signed by an engineer appropriately licensed in the subject jurisdiction. Reverence Engineering does have partner engineers employed for specialty or small-volume jurisdictions; all work is performed and managed at Reverence Engineering, but the final stamp by the licensed engineer may read differently.
3. The base deliverable shall convey the structural intent and basis for design conformance. The base deliverable is not a fabrication or shop-level set of drawings and will likely not include shop-level specificity and components not part of the structural system.
4. All features under a project request will be provided in one package unless requested differently before commencing work or if already part of a pre-engineered program. Separating features into individual packages will incur an additional fee after work has commenced.
5. Project estimates (when issued) are typical and based on information available at the time the estimate is issued. Estimates and services should be assumed to be consistent with standard industry service offerings for obtaining a permit. Special requests or requests above and beyond what is typical must be communicated.
6. Project estimates are based on an expected level of effort, experience, and time across various internal functions using one standardized company rate. Specific billable rates and time per rate cannot be broken out.
7. Project estimates do not include shipping, printing, additional copies, additional forms, shop reviews, or any other accessory services outside of the base deliverable unless specifically communicated.
8. Estimated project timelines are typically based on the presumption that the proposed design concept is generally adequate and all necessary information is provided at the time of award. Inadequate design concepts (which may or may not be apparent until a certain level of analysis is performed) or incomplete information may require additional time to complete the service request and may require additional billable time should the scope need to materially change.
9. Final service fees may vary with additions or changes that materially alter the work effort such as, but not limited to::
a. Additional client or jurisdictional requirements
b. Specific or atypical project requests or requirements
c. Additional requests or information that materially alter the work effort
d. Requests or information that creates rework
e. Peer review or plan check comments
f. Response Letters, forms, and other official correspondence
g. Meetings and conferences not specifically requested by the engineer.
10. The engineered design will match any provided shop-level or fabrication drawings as closely as possible where specific design information exists. Reverence Engineering will assume that provided specifications are purposeful and will not alter elements of the design unless code compliance, safety, or company standards dictate. Where specific information is not shown or otherwise provided, a reasonable engineered solution will be provided. 
11. Official plan check comments other than those stemming directly from errors or omissions as they relate to the contracted scope of work are considered additional billable. 
12. Reverence Engineering is not familiar with and does not research jurisdictional administrative requirements. Any administrative requirements affecting the base deliverable (such as formatting) must be communicated to Reverence Engineering. Additional fees may apply. 
13. Reverence Engineering is not responsible for the accuracy of existing or field conditions. It is the responsibility of the client to provide all appropriate information for consideration in analysis and design development. Where information cannot be provided or verified, Reverence Engineering may make assumptions about the existing conditions for permitting purposes at the direction of the client. Such assumptions may not accurately represent actual field conditions and additional engineering services may be required to address site conditions at a later date.
14. It is the responsibility of the fabricator and/or installer to verify all field conditions before procurement of parts and materials and before fabrication. 
15. Reverence Engineering does not “rubber stamp” client-produced documents. Should a jurisdiction require that client-produced drawings (ie, a brand book or art deck) be stamped for permitting purposes, Reverence Engineering must have already produced an independent base deliverable for each feature shown. Client-produced drawings must then be reviewed and reconciled to remove possible discrepancies. An additional fee will apply. Reverence Engineering will not modify documents produced by others; all modifications must be performed by the owner of such documentation.
16. Once a project deliverable is provided for review, the client shall be afforded 21 calendar days (3 weeks) to review the project documents. Before the end of the review period, the client may elect to suspend the project for up to 60 days; the client will be assessed a 1-hour reactivation fee at the then-current company standard rate to resume services. Should there be no meaningful progress by the end of the review period and/or the suspension period, the project will be automatically closed and invoiced for services performed; reactivation of the project at a later date will be subject to a reactivation fee plus any services to be performed to include compiling a final approved set of documents. Projects with an outstanding 100% review set will be invoiced at 100% of the estimated fee plus any additional services performed less any services specifically estimated and not performed.
17. This estimate is valid for 30 calendar days. We will make efforts to follow up via email approximately 3 and 10 days after the estimate is issued.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Hi Rocky,



I corresponded with the Town of Sahuarita concerning the status of the U-Haul permit application.


At this point, the Town is requiring the project to proceed through a formal Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) review process rather than continuing as a standard sign permit application.


The good news is that the existing artwork and exhibit package already substantially satisfies much of the CSP content requirements. The issue does not appear to be the design itself, but rather the formal administrative process the Town wants the project routed through.


The primary remaining items appear to be:
• Development Review / CSP application package
• CSP narrative / written justification
• Sign area calculations
• Identification and justification of any code deviations
• Owner authorization documentation


The current artwork package is likely already 70–80% of what will ultimately be needed for the CSP submission.

subject: 27808 CHANDLER FASHION CENTER FREEWAY PYLON
body:
Hi Andy and Monica,



Thank you again for taking the time to meet with me regarding the proposed freeway pylon concepts for Chandler Fashion Center.


Attached are the revised artwork concepts incorporating the updates and direction discussed during our meeting for your review.


Based on our discussion, I explored several revised tenant panel configurations and overall proportions for the scale of a 75’ freeway pylon. During the meeting, you wanted us to explore smaller 5' x 20' tenant panels and that felt somewhat undersized relative to the overall scale and visual mass of the proposed freeway pylon, so we shrunk the girth of the sign without reducing it in height to make that size of a tenant panel look proportionately correct. We also developed additional options utilizing 6' x 25' tenant panels, which remain smaller than the original concept while, in my opinion, providing improved balance and visibility for signage of this scale.




I also added accent lighting on the sides of the standing seam pop out to enhance the sign at night. I’ll get a night rendering of that for you next week.


The attached concepts are intended to provide comparative options for review and discussion as the project direction continues to evolve.


Please take a look through the revised concepts and let me know your thoughts, preferences, or any additional adjustments you would like us to explore. If one of these designs captures your attention please let me know which one so we can focus getting you an estimate for that one.


Thank you again, and I look forward to your feedback.

 Chad

Weekly Pool Service Report


Customer: Dane Christensen
Service Address: 14207 North 69th Drive, Peoria, AZ 85381 

Service Date: May 20th, 2026    Tech: Caleb
Service Time: 12:38pm



Service Summary:

Hello Dane, Caleb visited your pool on May 20th, 2026, and ensured it was well-maintained and sparkling clean. He performed essential tasks including skimming, brushing, emptying the skimmer and pump baskets, chemical testing, adding necessary chemicals, and backwashing. Caleb also conducted a visual inspection of the equipment to ensure everything is in good working order. During the visit, Caleb found that the free chlorine level was at 0.75 ppm and the total chlorine was at 1 ppm, which are below the ideal ranges for warmer months. To address this, 6 chlorine tabs and 3 gallons of liquid chlorine were added to balance the levels. The pH was perfectly within range at 7.6, and the cyanuric acid was at 30 ppm, which is on the lower end of the ideal range but still acceptable. Your pool is being cared for with attention to detail, and we appreciate the opportunity to keep it in top condition.

Hi Frank,



After reviewing the previous review documentation, I do not see these specific comments clearly identified in the earlier correction sets that had been issued previously.


The earlier workflow records and review status documents mainly reflected the project progressing through Substantive Review without detailing the current 2018 IBC Section 107.2 concerns now being called out regarding:
• mounting hardware clarification
• foundation details
• corrosion protection
• referenced engineering details
• fully defined structural connections


It appears these items were either:
• newly introduced during the latest review cycle, or
• previously internal reviewer concerns that were not fully documented in the earlier correction comments we received.


This is also the first time I’ve seen the reviewer specifically reference unresolved comments tied to Sheets 8, 9, 11, and 12 in this level of detail.


Given the direction the County is taking, it may be worthwhile to consider a direct discussion with the reviewer to clarify exactly what level of detail they are expecting for final approval.

subject: Update - Need An Update - Scooter’s 2597 monument sign
body:
Hi Alex,

 

                Do understand that.   There are limitations on ground signs thru Baseline due to an Overlay city zoning guidelines we have to follow to place sign.

 

 

To All,

 

Just reminder that current sign will not fit in the about 5’ -6’ average space behind sidewalk and in front of trailhead & maintain the 3’ set back required off trailhead edge, also need to be able to clear all in ground utilities.

 

The sign footprint is 5’-4 ¾” wide.     Per this BB, you would need to make a new very short 4’ tall by 2’-8” ½” footprint monument sign and then try to fit a 6’ wide gap between sidewalk and trailhead & be sure in that sweet spot all in groud utlites clear.  Then with landscape city required out front a short 4’ tall sign would not been seen.

 

Looks like the Average gap between the back of sidewalk and front of trailhead is about 5’-6’ range.   

 

Sign Code requires – Sign be min. 3’ off trailhead.  Or then you also will need a sign Variance to be closer than 3’.

 

The Trailhead somewhere along frontage will need to be moved further back into lot (need to pick a spot somewhere that sign can been seen still And clear all in ground utilities private and public for footing) by about 3’-4’ in order for current sign to fit.

 

Who will be applying for Trailhead to be moved?     

 

If trailhead does not get moved deep enough into lot to get the 3’ min. off trailhead we need, we will also then need after trailhead move process is approved, a sign variance to be closer than 3’ to the edge of trailhead.

 

Look forward to hearing from team.

 

Best,

 

Pedro Vargas

subject: Dig Safely Near Southwest Gas Pipelines
body:
DO NOT RESPOND TO THIS EMAIL. For any questions about your one call ticket, please contact your local call center.

STEVE SKYE,

THANK YOU for using 811 to submit a locate ticket for work near Southwest Gas pipelines. 

To help you avoid pipeline emergencies, follow these simple steps:

1.    Survey and mark your proposed dig area with white paint.

2.    Wait the required time. This is 2 working days, NOT including the date of notification.

3.    Respect the marks. Ensure all utility owners have responded before digging.  

4.   Contact Southwest Gas and request a monitor prior to bore operations or working within 10 ft. of high-pressure facilities. 

5.   Dig Carefully.  Watch this short video <https://www.swgas.com/en/excavator-safety?utm_source=link&utm_medium=website_email&utm_campaign=Damage_Prevention_Safe_Digging_Video&utm_id=Perseverant&utm_term=>  to learn best practices when digging around underground natural gas lines.

6.    Follow safe excavation laws for the state you're working in. 

Always dig with care! Damage to natural gas lines can result in costly repairs, service outages, and project downtime, as well as severe injury and/or death.  

To report a pipeline emergency or odor of natural gas, call 911 and Southwest Gas at 877-860-6020.

Thanks for working safely near our facilities.

The County is becoming increasingly strict concerning 2018 IBC Section 107.2 and is emphasizing that the permit drawings must reflect a “definite and complete design.”


The primary remaining concerns appear to be:
• Mounting hardware not fully specified for wall conditions
• Foundation details for the directional signs
• Corrosion protection at aluminum post/concrete connections
• Missing referenced engineering details
• General clarification that all structural / connection details must be fully defined on the permit set

Hi Steve, 

Thank you for joining the pre application meeting regarding a Master Sign Program amendment for the Hayden Professional Center. Talking points from the meeting include:


*	
	The Master Sign Program amendment checklist has been attached to this email. 
*	
	In the submittal, please provide an updated MSP package with a narrative that describes what is being amended from the original MSP. 
*	
	Please provide a site plan that calls out the total gross floor area square footage of the entire development project, this includes Night Owl. 
*	
	See section 8.511 <https://library.municode.com/az/scottsdale/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=VOLII_APXBBAZOOR_ARTVIIISIRE_S8.511FRSIGEPR>  and section 8.515 <https://library.municode.com/az/scottsdale/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=VOLII_APXBBAZOOR_ARTVIIISIRE_S8.515ALDECOINMIUSDI>  for all freestanding sign allowances.
*	
	Once all of the documents are ready to submit, you can use the following steps in SPUR:

	*	Go to Dashboard
	*	My Work
	*	
		My Plans for the application for plan number PA-470-2026
	*	
		Select the plan number PA-470-2026
	*	Click on sub records
	*	
		Click apply for the application in “Remaining Sub Records” where it shows “sub plan - Master Sign Program - MSP/CSP - Revision”.

body:
Ticket Status Notification

Ticket Information

Ticket Number: 2026051301206

Ticket Location: 9403 S AVENIDA DEL YAQUI
GUADALUPE, MARICOPA, AZ United States
33.36094040383, -111.962530211182 

Due Date: 05/15/2026 8:00 PM ET

Company: CHRISTY SIGNS

Phone: 6022424488

Fax/Email:  / STEVE@CHRISTYSIGNS.COM

 




Reason for Notification

Notification Type: Bore Standby        Date: 05/13/2026

You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path. 

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations. 

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a 

minimum of 2 hours prior. 

 480-730-3640

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .






Favor de hacer llegar al excavador correspondiente.

Effective December 31, 2012, State law A.R.S. Subsection 9-835 requires that no more than two substantive reviews are completed by a jurisdiction before the plans are either approved and a permit is ready to be issued, or the plans are denied and the review must start over.  With these limitations on plan review, the Planning & Development Department can no longer put plans on hold or perform a third review to allow redesign after the first review.  If any part of the construction plans are revised or redesigned after the first comprehensive plan review, the permit will be either denied and the applicant must resubmit, or the applicant may obtain a permit for the initial design and then submit revisions as a separate submittal.  

All Single Family Residential projects/subdivisions are exempt from this law if submitted for first review after September 14, 2013. 

Please visit our website for more information: https://www.phoenix.gov/pddsite/Pages/pddlicensetimes.aspx.

9. Final service fees may vary with additions or changes that materially alter the work effort such as, but not limited to::
a. Additional client or jurisdictional requirements
b. Specific or atypical project requests or requirements
c. Additional requests or information that materially alter the work effort
d. Requests or information that creates rework
e. Peer review or plan check comments
f. Response Letters, forms, and other official correspondence
g. Meetings and conferences not specifically requested by the engineer.
10. The engineered design will match any provided shop-level or fabrication drawings as closely as possible where specific design information exists. Reverence Engineering will assume that provided specifications are purposeful and will not alter elements of the design unless code compliance, safety, or company standards dictate. Where specific information is not shown or otherwise provided, a reasonable engineered solution will be provided. 
11. Official plan check comments other than those stemming directly from errors or omissions as they relate to the contracted scope of work are considered additional billable. 
12. Reverence Engineering is not familiar with and does not research jurisdictional administrative requirements. Any administrative requirements affecting the base deliverable (such as formatting) must be communicated to Reverence Engineering. Additional fees may apply. 
13. Reverence Engineering is not responsible for the accuracy of existing or field conditions. It is the responsibility of the client to provide all appropriate information for consideration in analysis and design development. Such assumptions may not accurately represent actual field conditions and additional engineering services may be required to address site conditions at a later date.
14. It is the responsibility of the fabricator and/or installer to verify all field conditions before procurement of parts and materials and before fabrication. 
15. Reverence Engineering does not “rubber stamp” client-produced documents. Should a jurisdiction require that client-produced drawings (ie, a brand book or art deck) be stamped for permitting purposes, Reverence Engineering must have already produced an independent base deliverable for each feature shown. Client-produced drawings must then be reviewed and reconciled to remove possible discrepancies. An additional fee will apply. Reverence Engineering will not modify documents produced by others; all modifications must be performed by the owner of such documentation.

I hope you’re both doing well.


We’ve put together our initial concept drafts for the proposed freeway sign at Chandler Fashion Center and wanted to share these with you for review. Please note that these are early-stage designs, and our primary goal at this point is to ensure we are aligned with your vision for the project.


The concepts were developed based on:

*	Our understanding of what the current Comprehensive Sign Plan allows 
*	The existing architectural and signage elements throughout the center 
*	Practical considerations related to scale, constructability, and cost 


You’ll see a few different approaches explored in the attached concepts (including variations in structure, panel layout, and overall form), along with a more developed elevation study .


That said, these are not intended to be final. We are fully prepared to refine and adjust the design direction based on your preferences—whether that involves materials, proportions, tenant presentation, or the integration of an electronic message center.


Your feedback at this stage will be extremely valuable in helping us dial in the right direction, so we can move forward confidently and prepare a detailed proposal and pricing.

The baskets were emptied, and a complete chemical test was conducted. Your pool's water chemistry looks excellent. The free and total chlorine levels are both at 5 ppm, which is at the top of the ideal range, ensuring effective sanitization. The pH level is at 7.2, perfectly balancing the lower end of the ideal range. Cyanuric Acid is at 30 ppm, and Total Alkalinity is at 80 ppm, both within optimal levels. Calcium Hardness reads at 350 ppm, which is well within the ideal range. During the visit, Caleb added 4 chlorine tabs and 2 gallons of liquid chlorine to maintain these ideal conditions. All equipment was checked, and everything is functioning properly. Your pool is being carefully maintained, and everything is looking great!

Your permit is now in Issued status, and the approved plans and documents are available online through the Citizen Self-Service (CSS) Portal. Inspections can be scheduled online through the portal. Please follow the instructions below to access, print your permit, and download approved plans.

 

How to Print a Permit 

1.	Log in to the CSS Portal: City of Buckeye <https://egselfservice.buckeyeaz.gov/energov_prod/selfservice#/home>  

	*	Note: Registration is required to access records. If you do not have an account, you must create one before proceeding.

2.	Locate Your Permit: 

	*	Click on the “Dashboard” tab.
	*	Find your permits under “My Permits”, or use the search bar to locate them.
	*	Click the permit record to open the permit details.

3.	Print the Permit: 

	*	Locate and Click the Printer Icon at the top right section of the screen.

 



 

How to Download Approved Plans

1.	Access the Permit Record (Follow Steps 1-2 above)
2.	Go to the “Attachments” tab within the permit record.
3.	Click on each approved file to download.

 

Important Notes:

*	You must be logged in to access permit documents and schedule inspections.
*	If you cannot view your records, please email permitcenter@buckeyeaz.gov <mailto:permitcenter@buckeyeaz.gov>  or call our office at 623-349-6200 for assistance.

We received correction comments back from the City of Phoenix on the Senita on Cave Creek project (see below).


The main issues are related to Code 705 (multifamily signage, see sign code attached):

*	Height: The proposed sign location on the tower exceeds the maximum allowed height of 15’ to top of sign. The current design places the sign well above that limit. 
*	Area: The sign also exceeds the maximum allowable sign area of 47.75 SF for this use. 


The city has indicated the only alternatives are to revise the sign to comply or pursue a variance. Given the cost, timeline, and burden of proof required, a variance is not a practical option here.


At this point, we will need to:

*	Lower the sign location to within the 15’ height limit 
*	Adjust the sign size and/or configuration to meet allowable area 


Let me know if able to be of any additional assistance.

Hi Scott,




We received correction comments from the Town of Gilbert on the First Watch #54530 sign permit application along with the applicable Crossroads Towne Center CSP requirements (see attached).  Below is a summary of what the reviewer is asking for:




• Elevation / Sign Band Information
They are requesting the length of each building elevation and the dimensions of the sign band area so they can verify the allowable sign area and confirm the 75% coverage limit required by the CSP.

• ASA / Frontage Calculation
The reviewer noted the allowable sign area must be calculated based on the storefront frontage per the CSP criteria and documented on the plans.

• Raceway Detail
The canopy letter detail shows an exposed raceway, and the CSP requires all electrical components to be concealed. They want that detail revised accordingly.


That’s the full scope of the comments — nothing unusual or outside typical CSP compliance documentation. Once the drawings are updated to reflect these items, we can proceed with the resubmittal.

Hi Andy and Monica,

I hope you’re both doing well.


We’ve put together our initial concept drafts for the proposed freeway sign at Chandler Fashion Center and wanted to share these with you for review. Please note that these are early-stage designs, and our primary goal at this point is to ensure we are aligned with your vision for the project.


The concepts were developed based on:

*	Our understanding of what the current Comprehensive Sign Plan allows 
*	The existing architectural and signage elements throughout the center 
*	Practical considerations related to scale, constructability, and cost 


You’ll see a few different approaches explored in the attached concepts (including variations in structure, panel layout, and overall form), along with a more developed elevation study .


That said, these are not intended to be final. We are fully prepared to refine and adjust the design direction based on your preferences—whether that involves materials, proportions, tenant presentation, or the integration of an electronic message center.


Your feedback at this stage will be extremely valuable in helping us dial in the right direction, so we can move forward confidently and prepare a detailed proposal and pricing.

Thank you again—we appreciate the opportunity to work with you on this.

Cc: Chad Keller <chad@christysigns.com>
Subject: [EXT]: Chandler Fashion Center – Freeway Sign Concept Drafts (05/01/26)

 

Hi Andy and Monica,

I hope you’re both doing well.


We’ve put together our initial concept drafts for the proposed freeway sign at Chandler Fashion Center and wanted to share these with you for review. Please note that these are early-stage designs, and our primary goal at this point is to ensure we are aligned with your vision for the project.


The concepts were developed based on:

*	Our understanding of what the current Comprehensive Sign Plan allows 
*	The existing architectural and signage elements throughout the center 
*	Practical considerations related to scale, constructability, and cost 


You’ll see a few different approaches explored in the attached concepts (including variations in structure, panel layout, and overall form), along with a more developed elevation study .


That said, these are not intended to be final. We are fully prepared to refine and adjust the design direction based on your preferences—whether that involves materials, proportions, tenant presentation, or the integration of an electronic message center.


Your feedback at this stage will be extremely valuable in helping us dial in the right direction, so we can move forward confidently and prepare a detailed proposal and pricing.


We look forward to hearing your thoughts and would be happy to schedule a time to walk through the concepts together.


Thank you again—we appreciate the opportunity to work with you on this.


Best regards,

 

Steve Skye

I reached out to the City of Mesa today and confirmed that Michele Large is the assigned reviewer on this project. I left her a voicemail and have included her here so we can coordinate directly on this clarification.


We are looking for guidance on the illumination requirement noted in the review comments, specifically:

• For a remote letterset wall sign (no background panel), is the building façade considered the “background”?
• Does the requirement that “only the sign copy be illuminated” limit illumination strictly to the text (“Clayton Homes”)?
• Would the chevron/logo element be permitted to be illuminated, or should it remain non-illuminated (or halo-lit only)?


We reviewed Section 11-43-2 of the Mesa sign code, which appears to address internally illuminated signs with opaque backgrounds. Since this is a remote letterset, we want to ensure we are interpreting the requirement correctly before proceeding with any revisions.


For now, we recommend holding on any design changes until we receive confirmation from Ms. Large to avoid unnecessary rework.

Thank you for following up.


Based on feedback from Pinal County, a Comprehensive Sign Review (CSR) is required for this project. This is a separate application from the sign permit and is necessary due to the scope of the proposed signage.


We have begun reviewing the CSR requirements and are currently evaluating the scope of work needed to prepare and submit the application. Once that review is complete, we will provide an estimate for the additional effort required to process and obtain CSR approval.


Please note that the CSR will need to be processed under a separate order, as it is outside the original permit scope. In addition, the County application fee of $1,187.00 must be paid upfront to initiate the review process.


For reference, our CSR scope will include:
• Preparation of a justification narrative describing the signage and design intent
• Compilation of a complete sign package (all proposed signage, sizes, and details)
• Site plan and building elevations showing sign locations
• Documentation of any existing signage on the property
• Coordination with property ownership for authorization
• Submission through the County’s planning portal for review


Once the CSR is submitted and approved, the sign permit application can proceed through the normal review process.


I’ll keep you updated as we finalize scope and next steps. Please let me know if you have any questions in the meantime.

subject: Town of Gilbert -  SIGN-2026-00067 Your Permit is Now Available
body:
Your approved permit is attached. Visit our OneStopShop <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  portal to download any approved plans. These can be viewed under the “attachments” section of your permit. Approved plans and permit must be printed and available at the time of your inspections. 

To print a copy of your permit, please use the printer icon in OneStopShop to print your permit. If you do not see the printer icon and your permit is in an "Issued" status, please contact us at EplanBuilding@gilbertaz.gov. 

A one-time registration is required. If you have not already registered, please use this link <https://onestopshop.gilbertaz.gov/>  to do so. Please allow one business day following your registration to gain full access to the OneStopShop portal. 

You will also be able to request inspections as well as monitor inspection results. The OneStopShop is also available for online payments and to apply for future permits. 

For any questions, please call our Development Services team (480) 503-6700, Mon-Thurs 7am-6pm. Offices are closed Fridays and Holidays. 

Thank you, 

Town of Gilbert
Development Services
Ph: 480-503-6700

*We are transitioning online applications from our current ePlan Review to OneStopShop. OneStopShop online applications are currently limited to select permit types: Commercial and Residential Trade permits, Swimming pools, Engineering Utility Permits, Deferred Submittals and Plan Changes. All others must be applied for through our ePlan Review <http://general.gilbertaz.gov/eforms/eplan/BLDGSubmits/ePlanAppConst.cfm>  process.

Town of Gilbert
Development Services

1.) Measuring tape
2.) Copy of permit application and plans indicating proper distancing and location of sign 
3.) Phone availability of either Facetime, Zoom, Teams or another software program that will allow face to face interaction with the inspector.

subject: Phoenix Flower Shops Sign
body:
Steve..

 

Here are the photos of the sign. Prior to your team spot welding, you could rotate the sign so it would be parallel to McDowell Road. You had indicated this was due to the weld being broken on the base and that you would correct the problem and spot weld so it would no longer rotate in the wind.

 

It appears when it was spot welded that the sign was not properly aligned to be perpendicular to McDowell Road. It is now welded at a slight angle as indicated in the attached photos and does not look good as several people commented on it. This will need to be corrected prior to the skirt being modified and replaced.

 

Also, it appears that maybe new address numbers were not produced as proposed. I think they simply repainted the top portion of the sign grey and are following up by painting the existing numbers white once the grey respray has dried.

 

 

Thanks..

Ken

Hi Jacob,

Thank you for your review and for the additional insight — we appreciate the clarification.


We have updated the submittal in the portal and are including the revised artwork here for reference .

In response to your request, we have also attached the manufacturer schematics and product information for the proposed price changer units. These documents illustrate that the price panels are purpose-built numeric LED displays intended for fuel pricing applications, rather than full-color electronic message displays.


Specifically, the Optec Digit-PC units:
• Are configured for fixed numeric character output (fuel pricing formats)
• Do not support full-color graphics, messaging, or video content
• Utilize segmented LED digit architecture rather than pixel-based display systems
• Are designed for pricing display use only, with limited functionality beyond numeric values


Additionally, the attached shop drawings show the physical construction and configuration of the price changer cabinets, which differ from the full-color display unit proposed above .


Our intent with this revision is to clearly separate the pricing component from the electronic message display portion of the sign.


Please let us know if the current submittal satisfies the requirements, or if there is any additional information you would like us to provide.


Thank you again for your time and guidance.

Hi Jacob,

Thank you for your review and for raising this concern.


We understand the question regarding the display’s ability to present content beyond fuel pricing. The attached Fuel Price Display Narrative outlines the intended use and operational framework of the fuel price panels.


In practice, when operated in a static setting, the display functions the same as a fuel price changer, presenting fixed pricing rather than variable messaging.


In the same manner that the City’s Use Permit establishes how the display must be operated—including automatic shutoff at 10:00 PM, display timing requirements, and brightness limits not to exceed 300 nits—the static fuel price display is achieved through system configuration and operation.


We have also included Cirrus documentation demonstrating that the display system can maintain a fixed image, control brightness, and implement scheduled operation to meet these requirements.


The fuel price panels operate within this same compliance-based framework and are used to display fuel pricing only.


Please let me know if you would like any additional detail or to review the system configuration further.
