Jacob,

Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.


Thank you,

On Thu, Apr 23, 2026, 11:15 AM Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com <mailto:steve@christysigns.com> > wrote:


	Hi Chris,
	
	

	Following review of the County’s correction comments, we need to clarify the required deliverable for permit resubmittal.

	
	At this stage, the County is requiring a stamped and engineer scaled site plan that clearly documents right-of-way and easement constraints for the property.

	
	To proceed, please incorporate the following into a formal, permit-ready site plan:
	
	

	• Sealed, engineer/surveyor-stamped site plan
	• Property boundaries clearly defined
	• Future / reserved right-of-way (Miller Road) shown and labeled
	• All recorded easements shown (type and width, consistent with Schedule B/title report)
	• Required setbacks clearly indicated (including approx. 25’ from property line per MCDOT)
	• Dimensions from property lines to ROW and easement limits
	• Confirmation (graphically and/or by note) that structures cannot be placed within ROW or easement areas

	
	The intent is for your plan to clearly define the site constraints. The final sign location will be determined by Pattison ID and the client based on visibility, electrical access, and site considerations.

	
	The permit is currently on hold due to right-of-way and easement verification requirements, so this deliverable is critical for resubmittal.

	
	This plan will be submitted directly to the County and should be formatted and stamped accordingly.

	
	I’ve provided the correction notes and plans for your reference.

	
	Please let us know if you need anything further from our side to complete this.

	
	Thank you,

subject: Weekly Pool Service Report
body:
Weekly Pool Service Report


Customer: Dane Christensen
Service Address: 14207 North 69th Drive, Peoria, AZ 85381 

Service Date: April 22nd, 2026    Tech: Caleb
Service Time: 1:00pm



Service Summary:

Hello Dane, Caleb visited your pool on April 22nd, 2026, and ensured it was well-maintained. During this visit, Caleb performed a thorough cleaning, including skimming, brushing, vacuuming, emptying both the skimmer and pump baskets, and backwashing. He also conducted a visual inspection of the equipment to ensure everything was in good working order. In terms of water chemistry, Caleb found that the free chlorine level was slightly below the ideal range at 0.75 ppm. To address this, he added 4 chlorine tabs to help maintain proper sanitation. The pH level was at the upper limit of the ideal range at 7.8, and Caleb added 1 gallon of acid to balance it. The cyanuric acid level was noted at 20 ppm, which is slightly below the ideal range for cooler months. Total alkalinity was a bit high at 140 ppm, but calcium hardness was well within the ideal range at 350 ppm. Your pool is being carefully maintained, and Caleb is keeping a close eye on all parameters to ensure your pool remains in excellent condition. 

Pool Chemistry Readings

Measurement	Result	Ideal Range	
Free Chlorine	0.75 ppm	1 – 3 ppm (cooler months)
3 – 5 ppm (warmer months)	
Total Chlorine	0.75 ppm	1 – 3 ppm (cooler months)
3 – 5 ppm (warmer months)	
pH	7.8 	7.2 – 7.8

From: Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com>

Subject: RE: [External] Quote Approval – PK-6731 NextCare (Apache Junction, AZ) (03/13/26)

 

Hi Anna / Sharon,

I wanted to follow up on the NextCare Urgent Care location in Apache Junction and share our findings from the recent site evaluation (see attached report) .


The LED retrofit portion of the work has now been completed; however, during the process it became clear that the letter faces themselves are in poor condition.
